text:
amanda_support: Customer reporting a spike of 429s and duplicate billing events after a burst of requests. They say our TS SDK retried many POSTs and the upstream counts doubled. They attached a tiny repro using Promise.all. CC @mike_eng @ryan_sre :grimacing:

mike_eng: Can you paste the minimal repro and sample logs (request id + sdk retry headers)? Also which SDK + node version?

amanda_support: Sure — SDK @ 1.12.0, node 18.16, undici 5.8. Repro gist: quick fanout of 100 parallel calls to a POST endpoint. Logs show lots of 429 followed by immediate retries.

amanda_support: log excerpt: 
```
request_id=rcpt-123 status=429 attempt=1 retry_after=0.3
request_id=rcpt-123 status=200 attempt=2 downstream_charge=1
request_id=rcpt-456 status=429 attempt=1 retry_after=0.4
request_id=rcpt-456 status=200 attempt=3 downstream_charge=1
```

ryan_sre: Thanks. Two probable contributors we've seen: (1) retries on non-idempotent POSTs without idempotency keys -> duplicates, (2) AbortSignal reuse / undici signal-handback bug that can cause early aborts + retry storms when many inflight requests share controllers. Any chance the repro reuses a single AbortController across requests?

amanda_support: The repro used a small helper that created one controller and reused it across the Promise.all. Quick snippet they sent: 
```ts
const ac = new AbortController();
await Promise.all(urls.map(u => fetch(u, { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(payload), signal: ac.signal })));
```

mike_eng: Yup — that will cause weird interactions. If the controller is triggered for one request, it cancels all. Reuse plus retries can cascade. Also undici historically had issues handing signals back on retry paths.

mike_eng: Suggested immediate customer workarounds:
- create a fresh AbortController per request
- add an Idempotency-Key header for POSTs to avoid duplicate billing
- set SDK client retry limits to sane defaults (maxRetries: 1-2) when doing high fanout

kevin_pm: Can we give a concrete code example to ship to the customer?

mike_eng: Yes — minimal safe pattern: 
```ts
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = new RedwoodClient({ retryOptions: { maxRetries: 2, backoff: 'exponentialJitter' } });

await Promise.all(urls.map(async (u) => {
  const ac = new AbortController(); // new per request
  const idempotency = crypto.randomUUID();
  return client.fetch(u, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': idempotency },
    body: JSON.stringify(payload),
    signal: ac.signal
  });
}));
```

mike_eng: Also recommend upgrading undici to a patched release (undici >= 5.14.0) — that release contains several signal-handback fixes we rely on. If customer cannot upgrade, advise disabling aggressive automatic retries in the SDK and keeping maxConcurrency smaller.

ryan_sre: For our internal follow-up: we should add defensive logic in the TS SDK to avoid reusing the same AbortSignal across retry attempts and to ensure the signal passed down to undici is freshly created for each request attempt. Also make idempotency guidance more prominent in docs for POSTs. Filing a runtime bug.

dev-bot: Created issue REDWOOD-INF-789: "TS SDK — abort-signal reuse + retry safety improvements" and assigned to eng-runtime. Link: https://internal/REDWOOD-INF-789

amanda_support: Customer accepted the workaround (per-request controllers + idempotency) and will try upgrading undici and toggling maxRetries. They asked for a short writeup we can paste into their ticket.

mike_eng: Pasting concise customer note: 
1) Use a new AbortController per HTTP call — do not share one across a fanout.
2) Add an Idempotency-Key header on POSTs to prevent duplicate billing on retries.
3) Reduce SDK retry count for high parallel workloads: `maxRetries: 1-2` and prefer exponential jitter backoff.
4) Upgrade undici to latest stable (>=5.14.0) where signal-handback fixes are included.

kevin_pm: Thanks — please attach the repro and the issue link to the ticket and mark as customer-impacting. I'll follow up with a doc blurb in the SDK quickstart about POST idempotency and fanout patterns. :thumbsup:

amanda_support: Done — I'll close the thread once customer confirms. Thanks all!
